# Phishing reminder

Several staff received an email this week that appeared to come from the CEO asking them to buy gift cards. The message was a phishing attempt. Nobody in the company will ever ask you to buy gift cards or to share your password by email.

If you receive a suspicious message, forward it to the security inbox and then delete it. It is not neccessary to reply to the sender or to warn colleagues individually; the security team will send a company-wide note if one is needed.

Staff who have already clicked a link should change there password immediately and let the security team know. There is no penalty for reporting a mistake, and reporting quickly is what stops it spreading.

labels.notes: Misspelling plus there/their. "There is no penalty" in the same block is correct.
